Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Jordan Grant
Member ID: W874343567
Reference Number: POC-6A6D9C61F2-98168
Date of Notice: 2026-08-15
Requested Service/CPT: Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612
Appeal deadline per notice: 2027-02-11

To the Aetna Appeals Department:

I am writing to appeal the adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-15 denying prior authorization for lumbar fusion (CPT 22612), reference number POC-6A6D9C61F2-98168. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." This letter, together with the enclosed records, supplies the clinical documentation necessary to support medical necessity and requests reversal of the denial.

1. Governing policy

I understand Aetna applies Clinical Policy Bulletin (CPB) 0743, "Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion," to prior authorization requests for lumbar fusion procedures such as CPT 22612. I was able to confirm certain provisions of that policy directly. Where I quote the policy below, the quoted language is text I retrieved directly from Aetna's published CPB 0743 (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html). I was not able to retrieve the complete bulleted list of medical-necessity criteria that CPB 0743 applies specifically to lumbar spinal fusion (as opposed to lumbar laminectomy), because the source document is very long and was truncated before I reached that section. I am not quoting or reconstructing that specific fusion-criteria list, and I am not inventing any policy language, section heading, or effective date that I did not actually retrieve. I respectfully request that Aetna's appeal reviewer identify, in writing, the exact criteria section and language relied upon for this denial so the criteria can be directly addressed; the sections below address the clinical requirements that I was able to confirm from the policy text.

2. Clinical documentation responsive to the policy elements identified

CPB 0743 states, with respect to related lumbar decompression procedures, that Aetna considers the procedure medically necessary when, among other things, "[a]ll other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out," "[m]ember has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated," "[a]dvanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings," "[m]ember has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy," and "[m]ember's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression." The enclosed records demonstrate that Mr./Ms. Grant's clinical presentation meets each of these elements at the L4-L5 level:

- Neural compression signs/symptoms: Dr. Duval's exam documents neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, directly corresponding to the L4-L5 level.
- Qualifying imaging: MRI lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiographs dated 2026-07-18 show grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension views and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina — imaging findings at the severe end of the stenosis grading referenced in the policy language quoted above, plus objective radiographic instability (5 mm translation).
- Functional limitation: The patient cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force a stop, relieved only by sitting — a clear, objectively described limitation of activities of daily living from neural compression.
- Failed conservative therapy (exceeding the 6-week threshold quoted above): 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), 20 visits, from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03, per the physical therapy discharge note; 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-09 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. Symptoms have now persisted 9 months and have progressed despite this treatment.
- Other sources of pain ruled out: There is no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, and no other spinal pathology identified on imaging outside the L4-L5 level. BMI is 29, and the patient is a non-smoker, which removes tobacco-related concerns that the policy raises elsewhere for fusion candidates.
- No red-flag/urgent alternative diagnosis: There is no bowel or bladder dysfunction; the presentation is one of progressive neurogenic claudication rather than cauda equina syndrome requiring emergent intervention, but the severe central stenosis with cauda equina compression and radiographic instability supports proceeding to fusion in conjunction with decompression rather than continued conservative management.

3. Distinguishing this case from the policy's non-covered indication

I retrieved language from CPB 0743 stating that Aetna considers "[l]umbar spinal fusion for degenerative disc disease and all other indications not listed as medically necessary" to be outside the medically necessary indications, and background discussion noting that fusion for "spondylolisthesis for axial pain alone" is not viewed as adequately supported. This case is distinguishable from that description: Mr./Ms. Grant's request is not based on axial low back pain from degenerative disc disease alone. The request is supported by (a) objective radiographic instability (grade I spondylolisthesis with 5 mm of flexion-extension translation), (b) severe central stenosis with cauda equina compression, and (c) neurogenic claudication with a corresponding neurologic deficit (bilateral L5 sensory loss) — findings the treating surgeon, Dr. Duval, has determined require decompression with fusion for segmental stability at L4-L5, not decompression alone.

4. Requested action

Because the enclosed records supply the specific clinical documentation that appears to have been identified as incomplete, I request that Aetna:

1. Reverse the denial of CPT 22612 and issue prior authorization for the lumbar fusion recommended by Dr. Duval; or
2. If Aetna maintains that additional or different documentation is required, identify in writing the specific outstanding item(s) and the specific policy criteria section not yet met, so that the treating surgeon can supply it within the appeal window; and
3. Provide a copy of the specific criteria from CPB 0743 (or any other clinical review criteria) that were applied to this determination, including the section addressing lumbar fusion specifically, as I have been unable to confirm that language independently; and
4. Offer a peer-to-peer review between Dr. Duval and the Aetna medical director who reviewed this request.

5. Enclosures

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03, 20 visits)
- Medication/treatment records documenting 6 months of NSAID therapy and 2026-05-09 corticosteroid injection with outcome
- MRI lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiograph report, dated 2026-07-18
- Office notes documenting neurogenic claudication, bilateral L5 sensory deficit, and functional limitation (standing/walking tolerance)
- Surgeon's (Dr. Duval) letter of medical necessity
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office wishes to include]

This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-11). Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and advise of the expected timeframe for a determination.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Jordan Grant
